mistakes.subject: Physics
mistakes.question: A 1200 kg car accelerates uniformly from 0 to 72 km/h in 8.0 s. Calculate the net resultant force.
mistakes.correctAnswer: F = 3000 N (72 km/h must be converted to 20 m/s: a = 20/8 = 2.5 m/s²; F = 1200 * 2.5 = 3000 N)
mistakes.explanation: Did not convert km/h to SI unit m/s before applying F = ma (divide km/h by 3.6 to get m/s).

flashcards.subject: Physics
flashcards.front: State Newton's Second Law of Motion in words and formula.
flashcards.back:
The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the resultant force acting on it and takes place in the direction of the force.
Formula: F = dp/dt (or F = ma for constant mass).
Units: F in N, m in kg, a in m s⁻².

flashcards.subject: Chemistry
flashcards.back:
The energy required to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms to produce one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.
Equation: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻
Units: kJ mol⁻¹.

flashcards.subject: Computer Science
flashcards.front: State De Morgan's Laws for Boolean Algebra.
flashcards.back:
Law 1: NOT(A AND B) = (NOT A) OR (NOT B)
Law 2: NOT(A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B)
In symbols:
(A . B)' = A' + B'
(A + B)' = A' . B'

flashcards.subject: Chemistry
flashcards.front: Explain why H2O has a higher boiling point than H2S.
flashcards.back: Oxygen is significantly more electronegative than Sulfur. H2O molecules form strong intermolecular Hydrogen Bonds (between lone pairs on O and δ+ H atoms), which require much more thermal energy to overcome than the weaker London dispersion and permanent dipole forces in H2S.

flashcards.subject: Physics
flashcards.front: Express the Joule (J) and Newton (N) in SI base units.
flashcards.back:
Newton (N): kg m s⁻² (from F = ma)
Joule (J): kg m² s⁻² (from W = F × d = N × m)

formulas.subject: Physics
formulas.title: Equations of Uniformly Accelerated Motion (SUVAT)
formulas.equation: v = u + at | s = ut + ½at² | v² = u² + 2as | s = ½(u + v)t
formulas.symbols: s: displacement (m), u: initial velocity (m s⁻¹), v: final velocity (m s⁻¹), a: acceleration (m s⁻²), t: time (s)
formulas.conditions: Only applicable when acceleration 'a' is constant.

formulas.subject: Chemistry
formulas.title: Ideal Gas Equation
formulas.symbols: p: pressure (Pa or N m⁻²), V: volume (m³), n: moles (mol), R: 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T: absolute temperature (K = °C + 273.15)
formulas.conditions: Standard SI conversions: 1 dm³ = 10⁻³ m³, 1 cm³ = 10⁻⁶ m³, 1 kPa = 10³ Pa.

formulas.subject: Computer Science
formulas.title: Two's Complement Range for n-bits
formulas.symbols: For 8 bits (n=8): -128 to +127. Most significant bit represents -2^(n-1).
formulas.conditions: Used for signed binary integer arithmetic.
